game: CIN@DEN Week 4 2025 / kickoff 2025-09-29 20:15 ET / DEN -7.5 / total 44.5 / outdoor / weather not in pack

script.base: Denver leads at home as a 7.5-point favorite with implied totals DEN 26.0 and CIN 18.5. Bo Nix does not need a shootout; J.K. Dobbins (41 carries, 222 yards in weeks 1-3) gets the late clock work while Jake Browning, the only CIN QB in the L3 rusher list (2 carries, 4 yards), trails and throws. Pace is moderate on a 44.5 total, not a slog and not a track meet. CIN's already-broken run (Chase Brown 47 carries, 93 yards, 1.98 YPC) gets abandoned.
script.flip1: Cincinnati hangs within a score or leads early. Denver stays in dropback, Dobbins never gets the closer carries, and Browning-to-Chase/Higgins volume stays live the whole way, so dog rush unders and favorite RB overs both die together.
script.flip2: Denver blows it open past the 7.5 (a real snap-risk flag, not the base case). Dobbins can be yanked before 76.5, Nix kneels, and CIN garbage-time throws inflate Chase/Higgins/Gesicki while Brown's carries go to zero. Same direction as the base for Brown's rush under; dangerous for Dobbins' over.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report, not the 90-minute inactive list (not in pack). CIN TE Noah Fant Out (concussion): he was the TE target leader at 14 targets, 80 yards, 40 air yards over 3 games. Next receiving TE is Mike Gesicki (10 targets, 38 yards, 90 air yards, 3.8 yards/target) with Drew Sample (6 targets, 27 yards, 5 air yards) the short/inline option. Roles do not match cleanly, Fant intermediate vs Gesicki downfield, and DEN's tightest zone is the middle (5.48 YPA), so Gesicki over 14.5 is a sleeper candidate that fails the matchup/efficiency check and is not a leg. CIN DE Shemar Stewart Out (ankle): edge absence on a run defense already allowing 4.35 YPC and 7 runs of 10+, a direct bump for Dobbins, not a skill-position sleeper. DEN WR Marvin Mims Jr. Questionable (hip): 10 targets, 40 yards, 141 air yards; not ruled out, no practice trend beyond the tag, so Sutton/Franklin do not get a confirmed target bump.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, no MOFO/MOFC, no man/zone rate in the pack. Location proxy only: DEN allows YPA left 6.16 (44 att), middle 5.48 (23 att), right 7.88 (42 att). CIN allows left 6.57 (42), middle 5.86 (22), right 7.62 (47).
matchup.pressure: DEN blitz rate 32%. CIN EPA/db is +0.02 vs blitz and -0.54 vs no blitz, so Browning has been neutral under pressure and poor against coverage, which is about 68% of Denver's calls. CIN blitz rate 17%. DEN EPA/db is -0.33 vs blitz and +0.09 vs no blitz, so Nix is better when unblitzed, the look Cincinnati mostly gives.
matchup.bleeds: DEN defense bleeds to the right (7.88 YPA) and has allowed 8 passes of 20+ for 121 yards; rush defense is ordinary at 4.25 YPC with 5 runs of 10+, not a stuff unit. CIN defense bleeds to the right (7.62 YPA), has allowed 9 passes of 20+ for 117 yards, and is soft on the ground at 4.35 YPC with 7 runs of 10+.
matchup.overlap: Clean overlap is the run, not the uncharted WR alignment. Dobbins at 5.41 YPC runs into CIN's 4.35 YPC allowed with Stewart out. CIN's primary target Ja'Marr Chase (27 targets, 241 yards, 230 air yards) and Tee Higgins (14 targets, 104 yards, 193 air yards) would want Denver's right side, but alignment is not in the pack, and the middle, where TEs and hooks live, is Denver's best area (5.48). Courtland Sutton (21 targets, 185 yards, 300 air yards) has the explosive profile CIN has allowed, also uncharted by side. Chase over is not taken: median stand-in 50.5 matches games of 26, 165 and 50, the 165 is one-play inflation, and CIN's -0.54 EPA when not blitzed fights an efficiency over.

form: Avoiding season averages as the picker. Dobbins rush yards 63, 76, 83 (mean 74.0, 5.41 YPC); only 83 clears 76.5. Harvey 70, 8, 2 shows one long run, not a role change (13 carries, 80 yards vs Dobbins' 41). Nix is a real rush leak at 16 carries, 74 yards. Brown rush yards 43, 47, 3 (mean 31.0, 1.98 YPC) with receiving 8, 18, 17. Chase 26, 165, 50 is median-50 with one spike. Higgins 33, 56, 15 on 193 air yards is inefficient. Sutton 61, 6, 118 and Franklin 44, 89, 8 are boom-bust at their median stand-ins. Gesicki 14, 18, 6 on 3.8 yards/target. No similar-defense or prior-script splits are in the pack.

data_check.notes: No sims, no projection file, no Pinnacle, no no-vig. model_p is only the 3-game hit rate of the side versus the stand-in, not a calibrated model: Dobbins over 1 of 3 = 0.333, Brown under 2 of 3 = 0.667. pre_mortem: It's Monday and this slip lost because the 7.5 never became a lead-and-run game: Cincinnati stayed in it, Nix threw, and Dobbins finished on a 63- or 76-yard day that the stand-in already showed he can have, with Harvey or Nix taking the explosive carry. On the other leg Brown lost the under on efficiency, not volume: Denver has allowed 4.25 YPC and 5 runs of 10+, so one chunk play, or 12 carries regressed off 1.98 YPC, clears 43.5 even while trailing. A true blowout would have saved the Brown under and still killed Dobbins if he sat in the 60s. No wind check was possible, and a late Mims or Fant inactive change was not in the file to re-price anyone else.
slip_story: One script only: Denver leads, runs the clock, Cincinnati abandons a run game that has not worked. Stack is favorite lead-RB rush over (Dobbins) with dog lead-RB rush under (Brown). Those two win together. Do not add CIN receiver overs or a total under; those need a different or opposite story. No third leg. Gesicki was the Fant sleeper and was left off because middle-of-field is Denver's best zone and his 3.8 yards per target fails the efficiency check.
